messages.subject: Interaction Re: Miscellaneous usability questions
parts:
On Mon, Jun 27, 2016 at 12:46 AM, Gwern Branwen <gw...@gwern.net> wrote:
> 6. does blavaan support interaction terms? I am uncertain because
> while throwing in 'X + Y + X*Y' into the model doesn't break it, the
> output is not what I would expect.
>
> I've been creating a SEM mediation model of a self-experiment in
> which I investigate the effects of a randomized open door & bedroom
> fan on a sleep quality factor via CO2 levels measured by a bedroom air
> monitor (and also heat & humidity levels measured by two air
> monitors); the fan and door can be expected to have main effects where
> they reduce CO2 levels, but also a synergistic effect where the open
> door + fan reduces CO2 much more - hence, an interaction. My current
> model goes like this:
>
> 'SLEEP =~ ZQ.2 + Total.Z.2 + Time.to.Z.log +
> Time.in.Wake.log + Time.in.REM.2 + Time.in.Light.2 + Time.in.Deep +
> Awakenings + Morning.Feel
> HUMIDITY =~ Humidity.N + Humidity.K
> TEMPERATURE =~ Temperature.F.N + Temperature.F.K
>
> CO2.N.root ~ Door.r + Fan.r + Door.r*Fan.r
> HUMIDITY ~ Door.r + Fan.r + Door.r*Fan.r
> TEMPERATURE ~ Door.r + Fan.r + Door.r*Fan.r
>
> SLEEP ~ HUMIDITY + TEMPERATURE + Noise.N + CO2.N.root + Door.r +
> Fan.r + Door.r*Fan.r
> MP ~ CO2.N.root + SLEEP
> Mnemosyne.score ~ CO2.N.root + SLEEP'
>
> The output is not great since apparently 10k samples are not
> enough with the interim data, but it looks wrong:
>
> ...
> Regressions:
> Post.Mean Post.SD HPD.025 HPD.975 PSRF
> Prior
> CO2.N.root ~
> Door.r 0.048 0.026 -0.004 0.1 1.015
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Fan.r (Dr.r) -0.015 0.012 -0.038 0.008 1.024
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> HUMIDITY ~
> Door.r 0.029 0.028 -0.028 0.084 1.012
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Fan.r (Dr.r) -0.015 0.012 -0.038 0.008 1.024
> TEMPERATURE ~
> Door.r -0.026 0.031 -0.088 0.035 1.058
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Fan.r (Dr.r) -0.015 0.012 -0.038 0.008 1.024
> SLEEP ~
> HUMIDIT 0.311 0.460 -0.537 1.216 1.100
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> TEMPERA -0.060 0.533 -1.348 0.767 1.809
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Noise.N -0.208 0.214 -0.58 0.196 1.109
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> CO2.N.r 0.036 0.225 -0.381 0.471 1.024
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Door.r -0.067 0.036 -0.138 0.004 1.130
> dnorm(0,1e-2)
> Fan.r (Dr.r) -0.015 0.012 -0.038 0.008 1.024
> ...
>
> There's `Door.r`, which is the main effect for the door variable,
> and there is `Fan.r (Dr.r)` which is... the interaction term? And
> there is no `Fan.r` at all. This is true of all 4 regressions using
> the main+interaction terms. What's going on there?

So to follow this up: I wanted an interaction effect on
`Fan.r*Door.r`, since they may have different effects, and tried it
the usual way in R's formula syntax but got the odd results above -
only two coefficients and one is oddly named.

After looking into this again, it seems lavaan *doesn't* support
interaction terms although a `:` conditional operator is planned for
future lavaan releases: http://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html
Since lavaan doesn't have interaction terms, I assume blavaan doesn't
either; the blavaan paper (1511.05604.pdf) does say

> In addition to discrete data, we plan to support mixture SEMs, multilevel SEMs, and latent variable interactions in future releases.

but I don't think the discrete, mixture, or multilevel features are
there yet so interactions probably aren't either.

The suggested solution is, like with quadratic/log terms, creating a
dummy variable encoding the interaction and then use it as a simple
`+` in the SEM model code:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/HyNgkB73liQ/bLQPpquxxKAJ
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/ZhZTgJeADO4/0ou5SenRDgAJ
https://github.com/wmmurrah/lavaanFIML/wiki/4.-Regression-Analysis-with-Interaction:-Continuous-Moderator
https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/163436/r-moderated-mediation-using-the-lavaan-package
https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/60434/structural-equations-how-to-specify-interaction-effects-in-r-lavaan-package
Alternately, the ':=' operator can apparently be used but I'm not
really familiar with it or how it would implement interactions (the
'*' seems to be overloaded and I'm not sure what else changes):
http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html
The `indProd` function available in `semTools` creates such dummy
variables, so for my code I would do:

door <- read.csv(stdin(), header=TRUE,
colClasses=c("Date","integer","integer"))
Date,Fan.r,Door.r
2016-06-03,0,0
2016-06-04,0,1
2016-06-05,1,1
2016-06-06,0,0
2016-06-07,1,1
2016-06-08,0,1
...


library(semTools)
door <- indProd(data=door, var1=2, var2=3)

which creates such an interaction variable with the two variables'
names concatenated, and is used in my SEM like this:

CO2 ~ Fan.r + Door.r + Fan.r.Door.r

For my two binary variables, presumably I could also avoid using
`indProd` and have created it with a call like

door$Fan.r.Door.r <- door$Fan.r & door$Door.r

Either way, this seems to give sensible results when evaluated.

Where did the weird results come from? My guess is that blavaan sees
only two variables in that line and it's related to the labeling
function: the '*' gets interpreted as labeling the `Door.r` variable
with the name 'Fan.r', and the previous declaration of `Door.r` is
simply redundant & ignored by blavaan.

--
gwern

On Sun, Jul 24, 2016 at 10:07 PM, Gwern Branwen <gw...@gwern.net> wrote:

Where did the weird results come from? My guess is that blavaan sees
only two variables in that line and it's related to the labeling
function: the '*' gets interpreted as labeling the `Door.r` variable
with the name 'Fan.r', and the previous declaration of `Door.r` is
simply redundant & ignored by blavaan.

I think you are correct here. All this model specification parsing is handled by lavaan, which must read the asterisks as part of a label. And yes, in the next version of lavaan, the ":" operator will supposedly handle observed-variable interactions. I have not yet looked at this in the context of blavaan, but I am hopeful that it will "just work".

Ed
